key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Progressive over weeks to months, acute decompensation possible. LOCATION: Generalized dyspnea, bilateral lower extremity edema. DURATION: Progressive, chronic with acute worsening. CHARACTER: Dyspnea on exertion progressing to dyspnea at rest, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, fatigue. AGGRAVATING: Exertion, lying flat, salt intake. RELIEVING: Diuretics, sitting upright. TIMING: Progressive worsening. SEVERITY: Severe dyspnea. KEY POSITIVES: Bilateral leg edema, weight gain, orthopnea, PND, S3 gallop, cardiomegaly on CXR, history of alcohol abuse or chemotherapy or viral illness. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT acute MI presentation, NOT pleuritic.
